video_goal: Demonstrate how to measure the voltage of a zinc-copper sulfate galvanic cell using a Fluke 101 multimeter.
required_subjects_and_props: Fluke 101 multimeter, red and black test probes, glass beaker, bright blue copper sulfate solution, silvery zinc strip, reddish-brown copper strip.

outline_steps.visual_action: A glass beaker filled with bright blue copper sulfate solution sits on a table, with a silvery zinc strip and a reddish-brown copper strip partially submerged inside.
A hand places a yellow and grey Fluke 101 multimeter on the table directly next to the beaker.
A thumb rotates the central dial of the Fluke 101 multimeter from the 'OFF' position to the 'V' with straight and dashed lines (DC Voltage) setting.
Two hands pick up the red and black test probes that are plugged into the bottom ports of the multimeter.
The left hand presses the sharp metal tip of the black probe firmly against the dry, exposed top of the silvery zinc strip.
The right hand presses the metal tip of the red probe against the dry, exposed top of the reddish-brown copper strip.
Both probe tips are held steady against the respective metal strips, with the blue copper sulfate solution visible just below the contact points.
The camera focuses on the Fluke 101 LCD screen as the digital numbers rapidly climb and stabilize at approximately 1.10 Volts.
The hands lift the probes and swap their positions, now pressing the red probe against the zinc strip and the black probe against the copper strip.
The camera focuses back on the Fluke 101 screen, which now displays a negative voltage reading, showing a minus sign before the numbers.
The hands pull both probes away from the metal strips and rest them flat on the table next to the beaker.
A thumb rotates the central dial of the Fluke 101 multimeter back to the 'OFF' position, and the digital screen goes blank.
